**Assessment: none of the three solutions gives a verifiable answer.**

**Solution 1 (12)** is not supported. Its counting is loose: it treats preperiodic points as S₃-orbits of size 3 or 6 without checking that the resulting map is quadratic, that its fixed-point and period-2 data are consistent, or that all the orbits can be rational at once. Its "$3 + 3 + 6$" configuration is asserted, not constructed.

**Solution 2 (4)** is wrong on its own terms. The example $f(z)=1/z^2$ has automorphisms $z\mapsto -z$ and $z\mapsto 1/z$-type involutions, so its automorphism group is abelian (about $\mathbb{Z}/2\times\mathbb{Z}/2$), not nonabelian. The claimed bound "the torsion of the unit circle has size 4" is also not an argument that covers all twists. Since an $S_3$-symmetric map has a rational fixed-point orbit when the fixed points are rational, the true maximum is plausibly larger than 4.

**Solution 3 (10)** relies on a classification claim I don't think holds. Quadratic rational maps have automorphism groups from a short list that includes $S_3$ but not $A_4$, so the "$A_4$ map" it names does not exist in degree 2. Also, the count 10 exceeds the general bound of 9 that I recall for all quadratic rational maps over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Doyle). If that bound holds, 10 is impossible even without the nonabelian restriction.

I could not verify the correct value from the reasoning alone. A check against the literature on quadratic rational maps with nonabelian automorphism group over $\mathbb{Q}$ (Doyle's work) would settle it. My best judgment is that none of the three is correct, though my recall of the literature is not certain.

CHOICE: NONE
